items.title: 490,586 join Social Security after immigrant regularisation
items.body: Spain's regularisation process has led to 490,586 foreigners joining Social Security. Applications closed on June 30, 2026, but decisions remain pending. An admitted application allows hiring while officials assess it; a final refusal cancels the work authorisation.

items.title: Spain's mortgage debt reaches a ten-year high
items.body: Outstanding home-purchase loans reached €530.218 billion in September, the highest in a decade. Higher house prices, fewer cash purchases, and slower repayments drove the rise. The average new mortgage is €181,285, up 7.7% year on year, INE (national statistics institute) data show.

items.title: EU recovery payment verdict follows November election
items.body: The European Commission will announce its assessment of Spain's final recovery payment, worth up to €25.861 billion, on November 30, after the November 29 election. Unmet conditions cannot be corrected afterwards. At least €260 million is expected to be deducted because the lobbying law lapsed in Congress.

items.title: PSOE pledges shorter working week and longer rentals
items.body: The PSOE's election manifesto proposes a 37.5-hour working week and talks on 35 hours. It also proposes longer rental contracts, a tax on large "vulture funds", and 1% of GDP for affordable housing. These are election pledges, not law; their fate depends on the November 29 vote.

items.title: Draft wage rise would widen unemployment subsidy eligibility
items.body: A draft SMI (minimum wage) rise would lift the unemployment subsidy income cap from €915.75 to €964.50 gross a month in 2027. Consultation closes on November 16; the government must approve the Royal Decree before it takes effect. Subsidy payments would stay unchanged.

items.title: Barcelona home purchases by non-resident foreigners fall 35%
items.body: Non-resident foreigners bought 804 Barcelona homes in 2025, down 35%; the decline continued in early 2026. Across Catalonia, foreign residents bought a record 18,064 homes, up 7%. The sector links weaker non-resident demand to scarce supply, rising prices, and Catalonia's market rules.

items.title: Spanish whisky makers collect international awards
items.body: Siderit's PX Cask Rye won world's best rye, and Liber's Toma 1492 won best Spanish single malt at the 2026 World Whiskies Awards. Ovalle won silver for Bateeiro Galician Wood and Ovalle Ruby Single Malt, plus bronze for Ovalle Gold Single Malt, at the International Spirits Challenge. Spain has more than 25 distilleries.

items.title: Fresh berries lead sharp food price rises
items.body: Fresh berries cost 54.2% more in October than a year earlier, while fruiting vegetables such as tomatoes rose 20.8%, INE CPI data show. Eggs rose 7.1%. Coffee fell 4.5%, chocolate and cocoa 4.4%, and sugar 4.3%.

items.title: Christmas road transport strike called over retirement delays
items.body: The freight employers' group CETM confirms it received notice of a CC OO strike on December 23 and 24 over delayed early-retirement rules for truck and bus drivers. CC OO has yet to confirm details officially, and UGT has not announced support. Deliveries and bus services could face disruption.

items.title: Nolotil study raises safety questions in Alicante
items.body: An unpublished 2019 study linked nine deaths in Alicante province in 2016-2017 to agranulocytosis caused by metamizol, sold as Nolotil; seven were British. Spain's medicines agency AEMPS says the report cannot calculate relative risks and that evidence cannot confirm or rule out higher risk in some groups. It says benefits still outweigh risks.

items.title: England ends Spain's 44-match unbeaten football run
items.body: Spain lost 3-2 to England in the Nations League at the Metropolitano on November 15, ending a 44-match unbeaten run. Spain fought back from 3-0 down but could not equalise. The team enters the quarter-final draw as a second seed and will play the second leg away.

items.title: Digital bank deposits nearly quadruple in Spain
items.body: Digital bank deposits rose from €20.349 billion in 2008 to €80.329 billion in 2024, a Funcas study finds. Growth accelerated in 2022-2024, when some digital banks offered better savings rates than traditional banks. Their share of total bank deposits rose from 3.8% to 9.4%.

items.title: Spain's population approaches a record 50 million
items.body: Spain's population is around a record 50 million, with immigration helping drive growth as births fall. An El Mundo podcast asks how Spain will handle an ageing population and the retirement of the baby-boom generation.
